name: South Kasai
alt: Autonomous Mining State of South Kasai

predecessors.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
predecessors.text: south-eastern Kasai: Kalonji 'declared the region of south-eastern Kasai to be the new Mining State'; the declared borders 'included all of Kasai Province except Sankuru District and Lulua District'…

successors.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
successors.text: Bakwanga (Mbuji-Mayi) and its surroundings, entered by central government troops on 5 October 1962

ledger.x: 1960: Albert Kalonji declares the Mining State of South Kasai.
1961: Kalonji takes the royal title Mulopwe (16 July 1961, after his father's 12 April bestowal) and 'the state's title then changed to the Federated Kingdom of South Kasai'.
1962: the central army returns to Bakwanga and the secession ends.
5 October 1962: South Kasai ends; its land passes to the Congo (identity.successors).

wars.name: South Kasai secession in the Congo Crisis
wars.outcome: ANC soldiers arrived in Bakwanga on 27 August 1960 and in the massacres 'around 3,000 Baluba were killed' ('a case of incipient genocide', Hammarskjöld); the state survived until the coup of 29-30 September and the army's return on 5 October 1962.

certainty.note: The declared border (Kasai Province less Sankuru and Lulua districts) was larger than the land the Kalonjists held; the pages give no map of the held land.
